title: Staying two weeks that became fourteen years with Basie
summary: Returning for his drums, he is talked into staying; he told Basie he'd play two weeks until a drummer was found, and it lasted 14 years.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now you're in the band now, right?
You joined them in Kansas City - were you there when Fletcher was there?
I didn't join them. I come back to pick up my drums with Jimmy Jewell that - where you played all the dances at the Dreamland Ballroom and they told me, you can't leave. Ben Webster and
all of them stopped you from going, so you stayed, huh?

I came back to pick up my drums, Milt, and they had given me two quarts of whiskey and I went over to the rooming house and the guitar player and Basie was there. I gave them this two quarts of whiskey and I said, "I'm picking up my drums because I'm going back to school. I won't be playing in no band." And Ben Webster When Lester wanted to slap me. "Why, are you crazy?" And Herschel Evans says, "You're crazy. You can play in the band." I said, "No I can't." So I said, "All right, Mr. Basie, I will play with you for two weeks until you find a drummer." That lasted 14 years and I'm still with him. I went to the Union; I went to the President; I went to the Secretary and I wrote it out on a piece of paper: I will play with you for 2 weeks until you find a drummer.
